commitments.ndc_target: 45.5% reduction in GHG emissions below BAU by 2030 (18.3% unconditional, 27.2% conditional on international finance)
key_laws: Framework Law 99-12 on the National Charter for Environment and Sustainable Development (2014)
National Energy Strategy 2030 (52% renewable electricity target)
Green Hydrogen Offer / Morocco Offer (2024) — national framework for green H2 export
National Water Plan 2020–2050 and Emergency Water Programme (2020, extended 2023)

climate.rationale: Low per-capita emissions (~2.5 tCO2e) and a genuine renewables story — Noor Ouarzazate is one of the world's largest CSP complexes, and the 52% renewable electricity target for 2030 is a credible north star. CAT rates Morocco 'Almost sufficient', one of the few such ratings globally. But coal still supplies ~60% of electricity via Jorf Lasfar and Safi, and absolute emissions are still rising ~6.5% over 5 years as industry and transport grow.

forests_land.rationale: Forest cover is ~12.7% (mainly cedar, cork oak, argan), under chronic pressure from overgrazing, fuelwood collection, and climate-driven drought. The Forêts du Maroc 2020–2030 strategy targets restoration of 600,000 ha and a shift to community co-management, but enforcement is uneven. The 2023 Al Haouz earthquake accelerated land-use pressure in the High Atlas.

biodiversity.rationale: Not megadiverse but globally significant as a Mediterranean Basin hotspot with endemic argan woodlands, Barbary macaque, North African leopard (critically endangered) and a critical Afro-Palearctic migratory bird corridor through the Strait of Gibraltar. IUCN Red List trajectory is negative: ~11% of mammals and ~14% of fish threatened. Marine ecosystems under heavy industrial fishing pressure. [Planet Lens v1.1] Score = 80% Biodiversity Intactness Index (57.7%, NHM 2020, area-weighted) + 20% Red List Index (0.88, IUCN/OWID 2024).

protected_areas.rationale: Terrestrial protected areas at ~1.5% and marine at ~0.8% (Protected Planet), among the lowest coverage in North Africa and far below the GBF 30×30 target Morocco endorsed. The 2023 Biodiversity Strategy promises expansion, but gazetting and management effectiveness remain weak. Few OECMs formally recognized.

pollution.rationale: Urban PM2.5 exposure ~33 µg/m³ (6–7× WHO guideline) in Casablanca and the industrial corridor. Phosphate mining by OCP — the world's largest phosphate producer and reserves holder — generates large phosphogypsum waste streams and marine effluent on the Atlantic coast. Solid waste collection improving but landfill dominates; plastic-bag ban (2016) partially effective.

agriculture.rationale: Agriculture uses ~87% of freshwater in a country experiencing its worst drought in 40+ years. The Plan Maroc Vert / Generation Green strategies boosted export crops (tomatoes, berries, citrus, avocado) often in water-stressed regions, deepening hydrological stress. Fertilizer use moderate but groundwater tables falling >1 m/year in parts of Souss and Saïss basins.

env_governance.rationale: Unusually proactive for the region: constitutional environmental right (2011), an active Ministry of Energy Transition, and credible convening power (hosted COP22 in 2016). The monarchy's top-down execution delivers megaprojects like Noor but constrains civil society — environmental defenders in Rif and Jerada faced prosecution; Western Sahara governance opacity limits independent monitoring of Dakhla/Laayoune renewable zones.

top_gaps.dimension: Agricultural water use vs sustainable yield

recent_actions.action: Signed first binding green hydrogen export offtake agreements with German and Dutch consortia under the 'Morocco Offer' framework — ~183,000 ha allocated for H2/ammonia projects
Commissioned Noor Midelt I (800 MW hybrid CSP + PV) after repeated delays — adds dispatchable solar to the grid
Extended Emergency Water Programme with 143 bn MAD budget through 2027 — desalination expansion to cover 50% of drinking water by 2030
Approved extension of Safi coal plant operating permit despite 2030 renewable target — ONEE cites grid stability concerns
Ratified updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) aligned with Kunming-Montreal GBF — commits to 10% terrestrial protection milestone by 2028
Expanded avocado and berry export acreage in the Souss-Massa basin approved despite hydrological red flags from the Oum Er-Rbia basin agency

context.key_tension: Morocco exports the clean-energy future — green hydrogen to Europe, world-scale CSP, phosphate for global food security — while running its own grid on coal and draining its aquifers to grow berries and avocados for European supermarkets.
